### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | no prior-permission gate — AI use is permitted for support tasks (language/editing, literature search, coding) but must be disclosed after the fact; disclosure is a mandatory checklist item at submission and must appear in the Methods section. AI tools cannot be listed as authors. |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | The journal's own Author Guidelines page has a dedicated section stating: if authors used AIGC tools (ChatGPT, other LLMs) for any portion of the manuscript, use 'must be described transparently and in detail in the Methods section.' This mirrors Wiley's publisher-wide policy: AI cannot be an author; permitted uses are language/grammar polish, structural clarity, idea development, literature-search assistance, and coding support; authors remain fully responsible for content. No pre-submission permission request is required — disclosure is the enforcement mechanism, not gatekeeping. |
| **Source URL** | https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14679205/homepage/forauthors.html (journal-specific 'Disclosing the use of Artificial Intelligence' section + submission checklist row 'Disclosing artificial intelligence use'); general Wiley policy at https://www.wiley.com/en-us/publish/book/resources/ai-guidelines/ |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes. Accepts manuscripts previously posted to preprint servers, and authors may post the submitted version to a preprint server at any time (before or during review). Note: because the journal runs double-anonymized review, the guidelines explicitly warn that posting a preprint may compromise reviewer-side anonymity.
> Source: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14679205/homepage/forauthors.html

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Analytic philosophy spanning ethics, epistemology, philosophy of logic/language, and especially Wittgenstein scholarship — the journal is the official organ of the British Wittgenstein Society. July 2026 issue (Vol 49 No 3) contents confirm this: 'Wittgenstein On Moral Certainty' (Eriksen & Christensen); ''Mr. Preacherman, Should We Love Thy Neighbour?': On Moral Understanding and Moral Change in Deep Moral Disagreements' (Manhire & Salskov); 'Is Conventionalism About Logic Viciously Circular?' (Büttner); ''Logic Is Transcendental': Content, Isomorphism and Intentionality in Wittgenstein's Logic of Depiction' (Nota); plus book reviews of works by John Cottingham, Mark Hopwood (Iris Murdoch), Peter Winch (posthumous collection), and an Anscombe-on-Wittgenstein essay collection. Other recent (2025-2026) titles found: 'Moral certainty and the wrongness of killing: A non-propositional view'; 'The problem of free will is child's play'; 'Wittgenstein, normativity and the space of reasons'.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Analytic philosophical argumentation / conceptual analysis, Close textual and exegetical Wittgenstein scholarship, Moral philosophy / applied ethics essays, Philosophy of logic and language, Critical notices, discussion pieces, and book reviews
